title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-04-09
lineage: [SBD > MR > Cass > D > CD] + [AUD > MC > 4x Cass > DAT > CD]

ai_review.summary: Soundboard‑dominant recording with good clarity despite some audience bleed and audio glitches; the show shines thanks to the rare Cowboy Jam, a fiery It's A Man's World and an exciting Other One.
ai_review.review: The tape captures a mostly pristine soundboard mix from the early ’70 Fillmore West run, with the acoustic set sounding sublime and the audience portions adding just enough ambience. Musically the performance is highlighted by the quirky “Cowboy Song” jam, a standout rendition of It’s A Man’s World and an energetic Other One, though later electric material suffers from uneven playing and occasional tape problems.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the set 4–5 stars and praise key performances; recording quality is generally good with only isolated audio issues, yielding an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Acoustic soundboard tracks are described as sublime; audience bleed is acceptable. Several reviewers note tape‑related problems (dropouts, muffled sections) especially in later electric songs.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Starts with a crisp acoustic set, moves into the unique Cowboy Jam and a strong It’s A Man’s World, but the second electric half feels less focused and shows signs of boredom.
